prompt.context: Our client is BankCoCard, a US credit card subsidiary of the major international bank BankCo. They have a rapidly growing $16 billion dollar credit card portfolio. BankCoCard is interested in lowering their cost of funds for their credit card program by starting an online bank.
prompt.question: BankCoCard would like to know if they should start an online bank and if so, should they launch a savings or a checking account for their new online bank.

clarifying_info.q: Will they launch both products eventually?
clarifying_info.a: Yes — BankCoCard wants to launch both a savings and checking account, but their budget only allows the IT team to build one product this year. Whichever product is not selected will be launched the following year.

clarifying_info.q: How much will it cost to build each product?
clarifying_info.a: Both the savings and checking accounts are expected to take the same time to build and will cost the same amount: $10 million each.

clarifying_info.q: What is the current cost of funds?
clarifying_info.a: The current cost of funds is 4% for the credit card portfolio.

clarifying_info.q: Are interest rates expected to change?
clarifying_info.a: Interest rates are not expected to change for the next several years.

clarifying_info.q: Do we need to hold reserves against deposits?
clarifying_info.a: Assume all deposits can be lent; no reserves are required.

clarifying_info.q: Will the online bank operate internationally?
clarifying_info.a: The online bank will only operate within the US.

exhibits.title: Account-Level Data: Savings and Checking
exhibits.shows: A table providing key data for a single savings account and a single checking account, including average deposit balance, interest rate paid to customer, average monthly transactions/fees, account acquisition cost, and account lifetime in years.
exhibits.data: Savings account: average deposit $5,000, interest rate paid to customer 2%, monthly costs $1.50/month, acquisition cost $50, account lifetime 5 years. Checking account: average deposit $2,000, interest rate paid to customer 0%, overdraft fee revenue $20 per event at 10% monthly probability, monthly costs $2.00/month, acquisition cost $100, account lifetime 10 years.

exhibits.title: US Online Banking Market Size
exhibits.shows: A table or chart showing the current US market size (number of accounts) for online savings accounts and online checking accounts, along with market growth rates.
exhibits.data: Online savings accounts: 20,000,000 accounts, 10% annual growth (CAGR). Online checking accounts: 15,000,000 accounts, 20% annual growth (CAGR).

framework: Define the objective: lower cost of funds for the $16B credit card portfolio by funding it with cheaper online deposits
Evaluate the decision to start an online bank at all: strategic fit, regulatory requirements, build cost vs. benefit

Compare the two products (savings vs. checking) on: account-level profitability (revenue minus costs over account lifetime), total lifetime profit for year-1 cohort (account-level profit × market share captured), and strategic fit with the original funding objective
Assess account acquisition: channels and cost to reach target customer base

questions.prompt: What upfront costs will there be to launch an online banking product?
questions.guidance: Candidate should brainstorm infrastructure (website, servers, call center build-out), product design, employee training, and marketing. Good candidates organize into capital expenditures vs. operating expenses and note the $10M IT build cost given in clarifying info.

questions.prompt: What are the ongoing revenues and costs of a savings account? What additional revenues and costs does a checking account have that the savings account does not?
questions.guidance: Savings revenues: interest earned by lending deposits to the credit card portfolio. Savings costs: interest paid to customers, call center, fraud, marketing, statement mailing. Checking additional revenues: overdraft fees, account fees, interchange (debit card), ATM fees. Checking additional costs: debit card transaction processing, ACH processing, ATM reimbursements.

questions.prompt: What are possible ways of acquiring new accounts for an online banking product?
questions.guidance: Candidate should generate at least 4 channels. Strong answers include: online advertisements, search engine optimization, affiliate/partner marketing, cross-selling to existing BankCoCard credit card customers, billboards, event sponsorship/tabling. Cross-selling to existing card holders is a particularly strong insight given the parent company relationship.

questions.prompt: The online bank will lend the deposits to the credit card portfolio at a 3% annual interest rate. Using Exhibit 1, calculate the lifetime profit of a single checking account versus a single savings account.
questions.guidance: Candidate should build revenue and cost line items for each product over its lifetime. A strong candidate will ask about discounting future cash flows; interviewer should tell them it is not necessary for this case. Savings is more profitable per dollar of deposit but shorter-lived; checking has lower deposit balance but longer life and fee income.

math.setup: Savings: Revenue = avg deposit × lending rate × lifetime; Costs = (avg deposit × customer rate + monthly cost × 12) × lifetime + acquisition cost. Checking: Revenue = (avg deposit × lending rate + overdraft fee × monthly probability × 12) × lifetime; Costs = (avg deposit × 0% + monthly cost × 12) × lifetime + acquisition cost.
steps: Checking Revenue = $620 (using casebook formula: $20 × 10% = $2 per year overdraft, × 10 years = $20; $2,000 × 3% × 10 = $600; total $620)
math.answer: Savings lifetime profit = $110 per account; Checking lifetime profit = $280 per account. Checking is ~2.5× more profitable per account.

questions.prompt: Calculate the total lifetime profit of all accounts opened in the first year for both savings and checking. BankCo expects to capture 10% of the market for whichever product they launch. After calculating, are you suspicious of any assumptions or data in the case?
questions.guidance: Candidate multiplies account-level profit by (market size × 10% market capture). Checking wins on total profit. A strong candidate questions assumptions: capturing 10% of market in year one is aggressive; average deposit balances may be overstated; account lifetime assumptions; acquisition cost. Exceptional candidate recalls the original objective (lower cost of funds) and notes that savings deposits ($10B) dwarf checking deposits ($3B), potentially recommending savings on strategic grounds despite lower account-level profit.

math.setup: Total lifetime profit = (market size × 10% capture) × per-account lifetime profit
steps: Bonus — deposit base: Savings deposits = 2,000,000 × $5,000 = $10B; Checking deposits = 1,500,000 × $2,000 = $3B
Bonus — CAGR: Checking market CAGR = 20%; Savings market CAGR = 10%
math.answer: Savings total lifetime profit = $220M; Checking total lifetime profit = $420M. Checking generates ~$200M more total profit from year-1 cohort.

brainstorming.prompt: What are possible ways of acquiring new accounts for online banking products?

categories.name: Partnerships
ideas: Partner with employers for direct deposit offers
Partner with fintech platforms or comparison sites

categories.name: Cross-sell existing customers
ideas: Cross-sell to existing BankCoCard credit card holders
Email campaigns to existing BankCo banking customers

recommendation: BankCoCard should start an online bank and launch the checking account in year one, followed by the savings account in year two

Launch checking first because it will generate almost twice as much total lifetime profit ($420M vs. $220M) from the year-one cohort, despite the smaller market size, due to higher per-account profit ($280 vs. $110)
The checking market is also growing faster (20% CAGR vs. 10% CAGR), making first-mover advantage more valuable

Alternative view: an exceptional candidate may recommend launching savings first because the original objective is to lower cost of funds — savings generates $10B in deposits vs. $3B for checking, directly addressing the $16B portfolio funding need
risks: BankCoCard could capture less than 10% of the market in year one — 10% is an aggressive assumption for a new entrant
Reputation risk if the online bank has service failures or security breaches
Account acquisition cost could be higher than modeled
Product may not be sufficiently differentiated from established online banks (Ally, Marcus, etc.)
Regulatory risk associated with launching an online banking product
next_steps: Meet with regulators to understand licensing and compliance requirements
Survey potential customers to inform product development and pricing
Collect industry reports to validate market size and growth assumptions
Hire IT staff and begin product build
Design website and digital customer experience
Request additional budget to fund both products in parallel if possible
Build or contract call center capacity
